Visit note | 2025-03-09 04:30 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Nargis Akand, 61, female. Mrs. Akand presents today explaining that she is struggling with her shoulder; she finds herself unable to raise her arm fully, cannot reach behind her back, and has been dealing with a stiff shoulder for weeks. She mentions that this trouble started after weeks of keeping the arm still following a sprain in Noakhali. She works as a software developer and has a history of Hypothyroidism. She denies any recent trauma, neck pain, or numbness down the hand. On examination, shoulder lifts only to 110 degrees, with reduced external rotation, while other vitals show BP 125/74 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, and weight 68 kg. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued for her symptoms. She was advised to start physiotherapy, perform pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up is scheduled in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-03-09 04:30 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Nupur Mondol, 43, female. Mrs. Mondol returns for a follow-up visit reporting ongoing intimate discomfort, specifically complaining of itching and thick white discharge. She states that these symptoms started after a course of antibiotics taken in Sylhet. She works as a delivery rider and has a known comorbidity of Bronchial asthma. She denies pelvic pain or urinary burning. Examination reveals random blood glucose 5.9 mmol/L, BP 131/72 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, and weight 91 kg. Local examination confirms vaginal candidiasis signs. Assessment: Vulvovaginal candidiasis. Plan: a prescription was issued to manage the fungal infection. Advice given includes wearing cotton underwear, avoiding scented soaps, and keeping the area dry. Follow-up in 2 weeks if it does not clear.

Visit note | 2025-03-10 09:00 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Shathi Bepari, 58, female. Mrs. Bepari attends for a review visit describing a gnawing pain in her upper belly, pain that typically eases after eating, and pain that frequently wakes her at night. She notes this started after weeks of taking painkillers for back pain in Keraniganj. She works as a software developer and has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies black stools, vomiting blood, or unintended weight loss. Examination shows a pain score of 5/10, BP 132/74 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, and weight 80 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild epigastric tenderness. Assessment: Peptic ulcer disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid painkillers such as ibuprofen, stop smoking, and eat regular meals. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a stool H. pylori test.

Visit note | 2025-03-10 09:30 AM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Riad Faruque, 25, male. Mr. Faruque presents for his first visit complaining of persistent muscle cramps and noting that he works indoors all day. He explains that his symptoms began after months of night shifts indoors in Shyamoli. He works as a graphic designer and has no major comorbidities. He denies bone fractures, fatigue, or mood changes. On examination, his vitamin D level is 11 ng/mL, BP is 124/76 mmHg, pulse is 81 bpm, and weight is 94 kg. Assessment: Vitamin D deficiency. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to get 20 minutes of morning sunlight daily and eat eggs and fish. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat vitamin D level.

Visit note | 2025-03-10 10:00 AM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Popy Miah, 67, female. Mrs. Miah comes for her first visit stating she has been experiencing an irregular fast heartbeat, fluttering in her chest, and getting tired easily. She mentions these sensations were first felt while watching television at home in Faridpur. She is a farmer by occupation and has a history of Bronchial asthma. She denies chest pain, severe breathlessness, or dizziness. On examination, her pulse is 130 bpm and irregular, BP is 127/79 mmHg, and weight is 46 kg. Heart sounds are irregularly irregular. Assessment: Atrial fibrillation. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to limit tea and coffee, avoid alcohol, and report any fainting at once. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and kidney function tests.

Visit note | 2025-03-10 10:00 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Bilkis Hossain, 37, female. Mrs. Hossain visits for her first consultation complaining of itchy raised welts that come and go, swelling of the lips at times, and symptoms that started after a new food or medicine. She recalls that it started after eating hilsa at a family dinner in Banani. She works as a shopkeeper and has no reported comorbidity. She denies breathing difficulty or tongue swelling today. Physical examination shows about 25 welts on the trunk and arms, while vital signs show BP 119/82 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, and weight 79 kg. Assessment: Acute urticaria. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid the suspected food, keep a symptom diary, and go to hospital at once if the tongue or throat swells. Follow-up in 2 weeks with the symptom diary.

Visit note | 2025-03-10 10:30 AM | Dr. Shirin Akter, Pulmonology | Patient: Ranjit Sen, 36, male. Mr. Sen attends for his first visit reporting a tight chest in dust or cold air, wheezing, and coughing at night. He states his condition flared during the winter smog in Narayanganj. He works as an accountant and has a comorbidity of Essential hypertension. He denies fever or unexplained weight loss. Examination reveals SpO2 94%, BP 142/91 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, and weight 85 kg. Chest auscultation reveals widespread wheezing. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep the bedroom well aired, and learn the correct inhaler technique. Follow-up in 1 month to check inhaler technique.

Visit note | 2025-03-10 10:30 AM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Yusuf Pramanik, 73, male. Examination shows TSH 7.6 mIU/L, BP 115/83 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, and weight 90 kg. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep a regular sleep routine and eat a balanced diet. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat TSH.

Visit note | 2025-03-10 10:30 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Mostafa Bepari, 61, male. Visit note | 2025-03-10 11:30 AM | Dr. Shirin Akter, Pulmonology | Patient: Shafiq Mondal, 67, male. Visit note | 2025-03-10 12:00 PM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Rakib Miah, 44, male. Visit note | 2025-03-10 12:00 PM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Arafat Uddin, 53, male. Visit note | 2025-03-10 12:30 PM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Ishrat Miah, 62, female. Mrs. Miah attends for a follow-up visit reporting symptoms worse when lying down, a sour taste in the mouth, and burning behind the breastbone after meals. Visit note | 2025-03-10 12:30 PM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Shathi Mondal, 63, female. Mrs. Mondal presents for her first visit reporting constant worry for months and feeling restless. She explains that her distress has grown worse since experiencing job insecurity at a company in Kushtia. She works as a shopkeeper and has no history of chronic medical illness. She denies panic attacks, suicidal ideation, or psychotic symptoms. Mental status examination reveals an anxious mood, restless demeanor, and coherent speech with intact cognitive functions. Her GAD-7 score is 13, indicating moderate to severe anxiety. Other vital signs recorded during the consultation include a blood pressure of 129/70 mmHg, a pulse rate of 73 bpm, and a body weight of 61 kg. General physical examination is otherwise unremarkable. Assessment: Generalized anxiety disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued to help manage her anxiety symptoms. She was advised to practise slow breathing daily, reduce tea and coffee consumption, and start regular counselling sessions. Follow-up is scheduled in 4 weeks to review her progress and therapeutic response.
